u1-d01.focus: How can you tell something is moving at all?
What does 'relative' buy us when we describe 2026-XJ?

u1-d02.focus: Speed is distance per time — find the definition and one example.
Where exactly does velocity stop being 'just speed'?

u1-d03.focus: One sentence: how is velocity different from speed?
Read the graphs in 4.7 before we draw ours tomorrow.

u1-d04.focus: Which quantities need a direction? List three.
Components: how does one arrow become two?

u1-d05.focus: Which equation would you use to predict where something ends up?
Match each equation in 4.9 to the question it answers.

u1-d06.focus: Redo the do-the-math boxes before you look at the answers.
Same idea, different chapter: vectors on a supported object.

u1-d07.focus: Acceleration is a change in velocity per time — find the units.
Free fall is acceleration with a fixed number. What is it, and why doesn't mass matter?

u1-d08.focus: Problem-solving night: GIVEN / EQUATION / WORK / ANSWER on each.

u1-d09.focus: State Newton's first law in your own words.
Short chapter — read all of it. Why did it take 2000 years to get past Aristotle?

u1-d10.focus: What does a net force DO to an object?
Force causes acceleration; mass resists it. Find the sentence that says both.

u1-d11.focus: Write F = ma and say what each letter means.
Pay attention to the do-the-math boxes — we vary mass tomorrow.

u1-d12.focus: Practice night: three F = ma problems, full work shown.

u1-d13.focus: Free fall explained by F = ma — then what air resistance changes.

u1-d14.focus: Find the sentence that defines action and reaction.
Why don't action and reaction cancel? (7.4 answers it.)

u1-d15.focus: What is a force, and how does the book draw one?
The book draws the arrows; you will turn them into free body diagrams. No FBD section exists in this edition — lean on class notes.

u1-d16.focus: Equilibrium for MOVING objects — constant velocity counts.
Defining the system decides which forces are internal.

u1-d17.focus: Which way does friction act, and what does it depend on?
Friction, then pressure — both are force over something.

u1-d18.focus: Equilibrium means net force zero — find the equilibrium rule.
Re-read with tomorrow's problems in mind: what is ΣF when nothing accelerates?
Newton's first law IS the equilibrium rule.

u1-d22.focus: Preview for Unit 2: why the moon is falling.

u2-d01.focus: The apple and the moon are the same problem.

u2-d02.focus: How fast is a falling object going after 1 s, 2 s, 3 s?
How fast vs. how far — keep the two tables separate.
Why does everything fall at the same g? Newton's second law explains it.

u2-d03.focus: Mass and weight are not the same — find the difference.
Mass is inertia; weight is a force. Compute both for yourself.

u2-d04.focus: Write the law of universal gravitation and name each symbol.
Newton's reasoning, then the equation it produced.

u2-d05.focus: Double the distance — what happens to the force?
Inverse-square practice: predict the factor BEFORE computing.

u2-d06.focus: What is a gravitational field? One sentence.
Problem 53 derives g from G — do that one carefully.

u2-d07.focus: Weight changes with altitude; problem 64 kills the 'above gravity' myth.
Preview: what turns falling into orbiting?

u2-d09.focus: Two motions at once — which one does gravity change?
Independence of horizontal and vertical motion — find the figure that proves it.

u2-d10.focus: For a horizontal launch, what stays constant and what changes?
Three horizontal-launch problems: the fall time comes first, always.

u2-d11.focus: At what angle does a projectile go farthest?
Angled launches: components in, components out.

u2-d12.focus: What is centripetal force — and what supplies it for a car on a curve?
Centrifugal 'force' is the one that isn't there. Be ready to explain why.

u2-d13.focus: Why does a satellite keep missing Earth?
Newton's cannon → circular orbit speed. Problem 42 is the moon.

u2-d14.focus: State Kepler's three laws — one phrase each.
Elliptical orbits and energy conservation are the same story told twice.

u2-d15.focus: Escape speed and orbital period — the two numbers that date 2026-XJ's arrival.

u3-d01.focus: Momentum is inertia in motion — what two things does it depend on?

u3-d02.focus: Write p = mv and give the units.
Problem 54: show kg·m/s and N·s are the same unit.

u3-d03.focus: How does a force applied for a TIME change momentum?
Impulse = change in momentum. Bouncing doubles it — why?

u3-d04.focus: Why does a longer stopping time mean a smaller force?
Airbags, egg on a sheet, follow-through — same equation, three stories.

u3-d05.focus: When is momentum conserved? Finish the sentence: 'when no ___ force acts.'
Problem 64 is a superhero hurling an asteroid. Yes, really.

u3-d06.focus: Name the three kinds of collision.
Elastic vs. inelastic: which conserves KE? Momentum is conserved in both.

u3-d08.focus: Stick-together problems: one final velocity for the combined mass.

u3-d09.focus: Bounce-apart: momentum in equals momentum out, but now two unknowns.

u3-d10.focus: Momentum is a vector — what does that change for a glancing collision?
Momentum vectors add tip-to-tail like every other vector you've met.

u3-d11.focus: DART was an impulse delivered to an asteroid. Re-read conservation with that in mind.

u3-d12.focus: Impact damage is impulse over a very short time.

u4-d01.focus: Work needs a force AND a distance in its direction.

u4-d02.focus: When is NO work done, even though you push?
Work, then power — the second is just the first divided by time.

u4-d03.focus: Re-read with angles in mind: only the component along the motion counts.
Components again — the tool for work at an angle.

u4-d04.focus: Write the kinetic energy equation. Double the speed — what happens to KE?
Two kinds of mechanical energy; problem 46 asks whose frame of reference.

u4-d05.focus: State the work-energy theorem in one line.
Problem 54 (skid distance) is the work-energy theorem in disguise.

u4-d07.focus: Name three examples of potential energy.
PE = mgh — but h relative to WHAT? Problem 51 makes you choose.

u4-d08.focus: If g falls off with 1/r², mgh can't be the whole story.
Energy conservation for satellites — the fix for mgh at altitude.

u4-d09.focus: Problem 43: PE and KE trade places along an elliptical orbit.

u4-d10.focus: Find the law of conservation of energy and copy it word for word.
Three conservation problems: pick your zero for PE and stick with it.

u4-d11.focus: Rolling vs. sliding: some energy goes into rotation.

u4-d12.focus: Re-read: where is PE largest on a roller coaster? Where is KE largest?
The pendulum is a conservation problem AND a timekeeper.
Coaster + pendulum: height in, speed out.

u4-d14.focus: What does Hooke's law say about a spring?
Elasticity, elastic limit, Hooke's law — find all three.

u4-d15.focus: Re-read with ½kx² in mind: why is spring PE proportional to x squared?

u4-d16.focus: Power is work per time — find the unit named after James Watt.
Power, machines, efficiency: nothing is 100%. Where does the rest go?

u4-d17.focus: Re-read collisions with ENERGY in mind: which kind keeps KE?

u4-d18.focus: Heat is energy that moves — from what to what?
Temperature vs. heat vs. internal energy — three different things.

u4-d19.focus: KE scales with v² — problem 52 shows what that does to impact energy.

u4-d20.focus: What is escape speed, and what is Earth's?
Escape speed comes straight from energy conservation. Derive it before class.

u5-d01.focus: What does a thermometer actually measure?
Temperature, heat, thermal equilibrium, internal energy — four ideas, keep them apart.

u5-d02.focus: What does specific heat capacity tell you about a material?
Q = mcΔT practice; problem 61 mixes iron and water.

u5-d03.focus: Conduction: which materials do it well, and why?
Three modes of transfer, then what makes a good emitter and absorber.

u5-d04.focus: Why does temperature stop changing during a phase change?
Problem 61 is the full ice → steam staircase. Do it last.

u5-d06.focus: Re-read: temperature is average molecular kinetic energy — find that sentence.
Kinetic theory: what is temperature a measure OF?

u5-d07.focus: State the first law of thermodynamics.
First law is energy conservation with heat included. Adiabatic = no heat in or out.

u5-d08.focus: Which way does heat flow on its own?
Second law, disorder, entropy — why 'thermal pollution' is a relative term.

u5-d09.focus: What limits how efficient a heat engine can be?
Ideal efficiency from the temperatures alone — problem 55 checks a real engine.

u5-d10.focus: Atmospheric entry: a meteor is a radiator. What decides how bright?

u5-d11.focus: Newton's law of cooling and the greenhouse effect — both about radiation out.

u6-d01.focus: What moves along a wave — the medium, or the energy?
Vibration → wave. Find the definition of period and of frequency.

u6-d02.focus: Transverse vs. longitudinal — which way does the medium move in each?

u6-d03.focus: Write the wave-speed equation and give the units of each term.
v = fλ three ways; problem 67 is a radio wave.

u6-d04.focus: Problem 50 is a radar echo off an asteroid — our Day 15 in miniature.

u6-d05.focus: Why does a wave bend when it enters a new medium?
Refraction of sound AND light — same cause, speed change.

u6-d06.focus: When does diffraction matter most — big or small openings?
Huygens' principle first; diffraction follows from it.

u6-d07.focus: What happens when two waves meet crest-to-crest? Crest-to-trough?
Interference, then standing waves as interference with itself.
Young's experiment: the proof that light is a wave.

u6-d08.focus: What is actually vibrating when sound travels through air?
Sound is longitudinal. Problem 49 is middle C.

u6-d09.focus: What is the speed of sound in air, and what changes it?
Echo problems, then natural frequency and resonance.

u6-d11.focus: Describe the Doppler effect for a passing siren.
Doppler → bow waves → shock waves: the same idea at three speeds.

u6-d12.focus: Light is an electromagnetic wave — what is waving?
Speed of light, then c = fλ practice.

u6-d13.focus: Where is the image in a plane mirror, and is it real?
Virtual images — problem 51 (spider in the mirror) is the classic.

u6-d14.focus: Converging vs. diverging — what does each do to parallel rays?
Ray diagrams: three rays locate every image.

u6-d15.focus: Reflection of sound is radar's grandfather.
Problem 64: a laser pulse to the moon and back — the radar timing calculation.

u6-d16.focus: Hotter emitters peak at higher frequency — Wien's law in words.

u6-d17.focus: Earthquakes send both wave types; problem 55 uses the lag between them.

u7-d01.focus: Charge is conserved; conductors vs. insulators.

u7-d02.focus: Write Coulomb's law. What does it look like?
Inverse-square, again. Compare to gravitation as you read.

u7-d03.focus: What is an electric field, and how do you draw one?
Field = force per charge. Shielding follows.

u7-d04.focus: Electric PE, then potential, then capacitors.

u7-d05.focus: Current needs a potential difference — what provides it?

u7-d06.focus: State Ohm's law and rearrange it for I.
Resistance, Ohm's law, and why a shock is about current not voltage.

u7-d07.focus: In a series circuit, what is the same at every point?
Series: one path, current shared, voltages add.

u7-d08.focus: In a parallel circuit, what is the same across every branch?
Parallel: voltage shared, currents add — and why fuses exist.

u7-d09.focus: How do you reduce a combination circuit step by step?
Schematics, then compound circuits. Problem 58 derives the parallel rule.

u7-d11.focus: Write the electric power equation and its unit.
P = IV, then the two other forms via Ohm's law.

u7-d12.focus: What is a magnetic field, and how do you see one?
Poles, fields, domains — and Earth's field, which the magnetosphere day needs.

u7-d13.focus: Currents make fields; fields push on moving charges and on wires.

u7-d14.focus: What has to CHANGE to induce a voltage?
Faraday's law in words: more loops, faster change, bigger voltage.

u7-d15.focus: A motor and a generator are the same device run backward — how?
Generators, AC, and the motor/generator comparison.

u7-d16.focus: Earth's field deflects moving charges — that is the magnetosphere.

u7-d17.focus: Transformers and power transmission — why the grid runs at high voltage.
